title: Seller Performance Standing — Step-Down of Serious Policy Violations
content:
**Rule.** A serious violation, meaning an intellectual property, inauthentic complaint, product authenticity or review manipulation violation, does not expire in full when its first period of six whole calendar months from its event date has run: it steps down once, part of the points it still carries coming off as one points-expiry entry carrying the violation's reference and type, and the rest expiring when a second period of the same length has run. For the step-down, whole calendar months are counted by calendar date back from the handling date: a date lies in the last N whole calendar months when fewer than N whole months have passed from it to the handling date.

A serious violation that has stepped down keeps its remaining points on record until its second period has run, and a violation already reversed or fully expired never steps down.

The step-down is booked by Northloop on the seller's Seller Performance Standing record when it falls due; the seller does not apply for it.

## The life of a serious violation

| Point in time, counted from the violation's event date | What happens |
|---|---|
| Fewer than six whole calendar months | nothing; the full points remain active |
| Six whole calendar months have run (first period) | it steps down once: part of the points it still carries comes off as one points-expiry entry carrying its reference and type |
| A second period of six whole calendar months has run | the rest expires |

**Hypothetical boundary.** With a handling date of 15 September, a review manipulation violation recorded on 15 March has run its first period; one recorded on 16 March has not.

**Already reversed or fully expired.** An intellectual property violation reversed when the complaint was retracted never steps down; nor does a violation whose points have all expired.

## Booking tool: `book_serious_step_down_71a20607`

**Capability.** Books the step-down of a serious policy violation (an intellectual property, inauthentic complaint, product authenticity or review manipulation violation) on a seller's Seller Performance Standing record: the given number of the violation's points come off and are recorded as a points-expiry entry dated today against that violation, the rest staying on record. The active violation points shown on the standing record drop by exactly that number, and the entry appears in the seller's standing activity with today's date, the violation reference, its type and the points taken off.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`, under the tool name `book_serious_step_down_71a20607`. Each call books one entry against one violation.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `standing_id` | Identifier: the reference number of the seller's performance standing record, read from the standing record lookup. |
| `violation_ref` | Identifier: the policy violation reference number the entry is booked against, read from the seller's standing activity. |
| `violation_type` | Enum: the kind of policy violation the entry is booked against, copied from that violation's record; exactly one of `listing_policy`, `restricted_product`, `intellectual_property`, `inauthentic_complaint`, `product_authenticity`, `review_manipulation`. |
| `points` | Fixed format: the number of violation points that come off at the step-down, a positive whole number (integer points, no decimals). |

**Return.** A receipt with `entry_id` (reference of the new points-expiry entry), `standing_id`, `violation_ref`, `points` (points taken off), `active_points_before` and `active_points_after`. A returned `entry_id` means the entry is booked and the standing record already shows `active_points_after`.
